shape_hint: Lag screw (coach screw): a hexagon head with a flat underside (no washer face) on a tapered-point wood-screw shank: unthreaded plain shank of diameter d just below the head, then a coarse wood-screw thread (core tapering to a gimlet point) over about 60-70 % of the length; head is a low hexagon of height k and across-flats s.
notes: DIN 571 hexagon head wood (coach/lag) screw, nominal diameter d in mm (4,5,6,(7),8,10,12,16,20; '7' is a non-preferred size). d is NOT an ISO metric thread (wood-screw thread). Lengths 16-300 mm. s is the ISO-type 7,8,10,12,13,17,19,24,30 series. Head height k min/max symmetric about nominal. e values in the standard are minima. The US/ASME B18.2.1 inch lag screw table (1/4 .. 1-1/2) is different and not included.

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched all 8 sources live (200), parsed every table; matrix 9 rows x 8 value columns x 8 pages. No cell where a different value has >=2 clusters.
problems: STRICT merge of fuller+qewit and capital+fasteners.eu+boltport leaves da_max, k_nom (and s_min, e_min, ds_min in the worst rows) at exactly 3 clusters - thin margin; producer's 4/5 counts relied on counting fuller and qewit separately
Family label 'ASME B18.2.1 · DIN 571' but table is DIN 571 only (metric mm wood-screw sizes); ASME inch lag screw table is separate
d = 4,5,6,7,8,10,12,16,20 are wood-screw diameters (fuller prints 'M4'...; capital/fasteners.eu print '(7)' in brackets = non-preferred) - label convention: bare numbers, 7 is non-preferred
da role: only degademir words it ('Under Head Radius Length'); symbol da (transition diameter) kept, label should stay symbol-based
e_min is a minimum (standard e min), not nominal; fastenerdata e values 7.7/13.2/33.0 are minority
